data.claim: The review CLI accepts the global --agent (mirrored onto every subparser) but its --help hides it (help=SUPPRESS), so an agent running ddflow review from a shell cannot discover how to attribute the review to its as_agent name instead of a derived {host}-{tree} identity.
data.falsifier: Building the review subparser and reading its format_help() shows --agent AGENT in the options section; if it appears there, the help is NOT hiding it.
data.mechanism: Ctx.requested_agent = args.agent carries --agent through to run_review/_name_the_item, so the flag WORKS; only its help line is suppressed by _accept_global_options_anywhere.
data.probe: build_parser(); review.format_help(); assert '--agent AGENT' in help
data.probe_output: Before the fix '--agent AGENT in review help' is False: ddflow review --help lists --gate/--intent/--base/... but no --agent line (only ddflow --help lists '--agent AGENT agent identity...').
data.question: Does ddflow review hide its --agent identity flag from --help, so a shell review is recorded under a derived identity the caller cannot see how to override?

evidence.note: claim CONFIRMED: before the fix, ddflow review --help listed no --agent line (git checkout of _REVIEW_EPILOG without the --agent note); ddflow --help does list '--agent AGENT agent identity (default: host-pid). Shards the log.'. build_parser().format_help() of the review subparser contained no '--agent AGENT'. fix added the --agent note to _REVIEW_EPILOG.

chunk_findings.detail: The bug is that a shell `ddflow review` is recorded under a derived `{host}-{tree}` identity instead of `as_agent`. This change never touches argv parsing or the identity used for the lease warning or the recorded review: given `ddflow review` (no `--agent`, the reported case) the recorded agent is still the derived host identity. The new text claims `--agent` is accepted after `review` and fixes that recording, but no option or identity path was added. `test_review_help_names_the_agent_flag` only checks that `"--agent AGENT"` appears in `review.format_help()`, so it stays green while that invocation still records the wrong identity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/review.py:24

chunk_findings.detail: The added test `test_review_help_names_the_agent_flag` tests `review.format_help()` by parsing the root parser and finding the "review" subcommand. However, `--agent` is documented in `ddflow/surfaces/declared/review.py` inside the top-level command's description/epilog rather than as an actual parser argument added to the `review` subcommand. `review.format_help()` prints the help for the `review` subcommand parser, which does not contain the global option `--agent AGENT` added to the module-level command description string, causing `test_review_help_names_the_agent_flag` to fail.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py:106

chunk_findings.detail: The identity bug is unchanged. This diff only appends help prose claiming `--agent` is a global option accepted after `review` and that passing it records the review under `as_agent` instead of a derived `{host}-{tree}` identity. No argv parsing, subparser option, lease warning, or recorded-agent path was added. Given the reported case `ddflow review` with no `--agent` (and also `ddflow review --agent as_agent` if `--agent` is only defined on the root parser, which argparse will not consume after the subcommand), the recorded agent is still the derived host identity. `test_review_help_names_the_agent_flag` does not catch that: it only asserts the literal `"--agent AGENT"` appears in `review.format_help()`, which the new epilog itself supplies, so it passes without ever invoking review or checking the recorded identity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/review.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test still only calls `format_help()` on the `review` subparser and asserts `"--agent AGENT"` appears there. The string added in `review.py` is help prose on the declared command, not an argparse option on that subparser, so `review.format_help()` does not contain `--agent AGENT` and the assertion fails on both the unfixed and this “fixed” tree. A test that cannot go red-then-green on identity recording cannot close Bbf6e536827.
